The `use-market-listings-table.tsx` hook alone is 135 lines of column definitions.\n\n2. **Premature entity/query abstraction (153 LOC):** The feature has a full entity layer with separate files for each query hook, mutation hook, client method, and type definition. A simpler feature might inline these or use fewer, larger files. The `keys.ts` cache factory is 22 lines for 3 endpoints.\n\n3. **Context wrapper layers (85 LOC):** A dedicated `ListingSyncProvider` context wraps only the listing sync WS event—a single broadcast stream. This could be merged into the general WS context or kept as local state in the page component.\n\n4. **Notification duplication (38 LOC):** A specialized notification item for listing-sold events exists alongside generic workflow notifications. The toast logic (show-sold-toast) is split between the provider (44 LOC) and notification item (38 LOC).\n\n5. **Formatters as separate files (25 LOC across 3 files):** Small, pure utility functions (`format-listing-price-cents`, `format-listing-created-at`) are given individual files instead of grouped in a `utils.ts`.\n\n6. **Unused/over-engineered config (13 LOC):** A `config/` directory with types and constants for \"account filter\" logic that is trivial (one string constant, one enum).\n\n**Root cause:** The frontend followed a strict feature-folder + entity-layer + context-layer architecture without recognizing that the listings feature is **relatively simple**: fetch a table, filter by account, sync on-demand, cancel rows, listen to WS events. The `keys.ts` cache factory is 22 lines for 3 endpoints.\n\n3. **Context wrapper layers (85 LOC):** A dedicated `ListingSyncProvider` context wraps only the listing sync WS event—a single broadcast stream. This could be merged into the general WS context or kept as local state in the page component.\n\n4. **Notification duplication (38 LOC):** A specialized notification item for listing-sold events exists alongside generic workflow notifications. The toast logic (show-sold-toast) is split between the provider (44 LOC) and notification item (38 LOC).\n\n5. **Formatters as separate files (25 LOC across 3 files):** Small, pure utility functions (`format-listing-price-cents`, `format-listing-created-at`) are given individual files instead of grouped in a `utils.ts`.\n\n6. **Unused/over-engineered config (13 LOC):** A `config/` directory with types and constants for \"account filter\" logic that is trivial (one string constant, one enum).\n\n**Root cause:** The frontend followed a strict feature-folder + entity-layer + context-layer architecture without recognizing that the listings feature is **relatively simple**: fetch a table, filter by account, sync on-demand, cancel rows, listen to WS events. The feature doesn't warrant 874 LOC; it could be ~300 LOC with inline styles, merged hooks, and simpler abstractions.\n\n---\n\n### GENUINE COUPLINGS: MARKETSELL / LISTINGSYNC / MARKET_LISTINGS\n\n**Dependency Graph:**\n\n```\nremove_listing() [API]\n  ↓\nmarket.active_wf_id(steam_id, listing_id)\n  ↓\ndb.market_listings().wf_id_by_listing()  ← Check if workflow running\n  ↓\nif workflow exists:\n  workflows.abort(wf_id)  ← Abort workflow instead of direct delete\nelse:\n  market.remove_listing()  ← Direct Steam API call + DB update\n\n\nMarketSell::handle_init()\n  ↓\ndb.market_listings().update(ctx.task_id, ...)  ← Register workflow\n  ↓ (later phases call attach_listing_id)\n\n\nMarketSell::handle_activate()\n  ↓\ndb.market_listings().set_status_steam(listing_id, Active)\n  ↓\nlisting_sync.require_sync(steam_id)  ← Wake poller to broadcast\n  ↓\nListingSync::sync_account()\n  ↓\ndb.market_listings().filter()\n  ↓\nbroadcast ActiveListing[] to WS\n\n\nListingSync background worker:\n  every 5min:\n    for each steam_id in cold queue:\n      sync_account()\n        ↓ broadcasts new snapshot\n\n\nWorkflowDispatcher::step_completed()\n  ↓\ndb.market_listings().clear_wf_id(task_id)  ← Deregister workflow\n  ↓ (allows future removal without abort)\n```\n\n**Genuine couplings (required, not accidental):**\n\n1. **`wf_id` bridge:** Listings table must track which workflows created them so removal can decide: abort workflow vs direct delete.\n2. **`require_sync()` trigger:** MarketSell must wake the ListingSync poller after listing activation so clients see it immediately.\n3. **Status tracking:** Workflow sets listing_id and status (Pending → Active); sync poller reads status to build events.\n4. **Cleanup:** Workflow dispatcher must clear `wf_id` to allow future removals.\n5. **Event publishing:** ListingSync poller must be injected into MarketSell to call `publish_snapshot()` or `require_sync()`.\n\n---\n\nThis completes the exhaustive structural mapping. Key Technical Concepts:\n   - Rust workspace, edition 2024, resolver 3, REQUIRES NIGHTLY (`#![feature(impl_trait_in_assoc_type)]`). Service crate package name = `server`.\n   - Hexagonal: `api` (Axum HTTP), `rpc` (QUIC via shai), `sv` (business logic), `db` (sea-orm + SQLite repo pattern), `crypto`, `steam-http`, `protocol`, `util`.\n   - Workflow engine = saga: `Workflow` trait state machine, `Effect::{Yield, Suspend{state,wake_at}, Complete}`, `compensate()` rollback (default `Ok(Effect::Complete)`), retry via `Error::Retry{policy,source}` + `RetryExt::retry_with(policy)`, durable via DB `tasks` table.\n   - **The \"command vs projection\" design rule (the abstraction the user wants):** *A workflow is a durable command (multi-step, side-effecting, survives restart, compensatable). A poller is an idempotent projection (periodically reflects external state into a read-model).* Placing a sell = command (MarketSell workflow); tracking active/sold listings = projection (ListingSync poller). The poller is SOLE writer of `market_listings`; the workflow NEVER touches it; hands off via `ListingSync::require_sync`.\n   - **Dispatcher Effect→status (one workflow step per harness `tick()`):** `Effect::Yield(state)` → in-memory Running, then `suspend(id,state,now)` → DB Pending, immediately re-pollable. `Effect::Complete` → `mark(Completed)`; the persisted state stays as the PRE-step state, so terminal output must be carried by a prior `Yield(Done{...})`. `tick()` = `poll_once()` + `wait_until_idle()` (waits only on `tasks` table Running count; ListingSync worker is independent so won't affect it).\n   - **Auth-cookie mechanism (stack/auth.rs verified this session):** the `steamLoginSecure` cookie is attached ONLY for Categories present in the client's auth set, because MockTokenProvider returns no cached token (so a refresh, hence cookie, fires only when `require_auth` for that category is true). `sell_item` carries steam_id ONLY via this cookie → `Category::MarketSellItem` MUST be in the mock auth set. `confirm.list/details/accept` carry steam_id via query param `a` (independent of cookie).\n   - Steam endpoints / wire shapes (all verified this session):\n     - sell → POST `market/sellitem/`; Optional/default: creation_time, multi, kind(`type`), summary, icon, warn.\n     - Kind: type 1=Generic, 2=Trade, 3=MarketSell, 6=AccountRecovery. `Kind::MarketSell => confirm::Kind::Market(MarketId::new(creator_id))`. Перепиши ci на github`\n\nPorted `.forgejo/workflows/` → `.github/workflows/`:\n\n- **`ci.yml`** — `build-client` (yarn), `lint` (`cargo fmt --check` + `clippy --workspace --all-targets --features ci --locked`), `test` (`cargo test --workspace --features ci --locked`). Nightly via `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly`, caching via `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`.\n- **`build-server.yml`** — cross-builds linux + windows-gnu server binaries on release tags, publishes to GitHub Releases.\n- **`deploy-central.yml`** — ssh-deploys `central` on `central/v*` tags, preserving the `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` / `VPS_HOST` secret references.\n\n`RUSTFLAGS` is set in-workflow so the `mold` linker pinned in `.cargo/config.toml` is overridden — no self-hosted tooling needed on hosted runners.\n\n### 2. Simplify the workflow engine  ·  `2. максимально упростить … мощными абстракциями`\n\nThe pain point was the **global `define_registry!` enum macro**: it forced every workflow into one central `View`/`Kind` enum, so adding a workflow meant editing a shared list. It existed only to hand the webui a closed set of variants.\n\nReplaced it with a **self-describing envelope** (−203 lines in the engine):\n\n- Each workflow declares `const KIND: &'static str` and owns its own `View` type.\n- `view::View { kind, payload }` type-erases any projection; the registry is a plain `HashMap<&'static str, Handlers>` keyed on `KIND`. A new workflow plugs itself in by registering — **no central enum to touch**.\n- The wire format is identical — `View` serializes to `{ \"kind\", \"payload\" }`, byte-for-byte the same as the old `#[serde(tag, content)]` enum, so the frontend's `workflowViewSchema` discriminated union still matches. A regression test in `view.rs` locks the envelope.\n\n### 3. Implement listings — and define when to use a workflow  ·  `3. реализуй листинги … понятно для каких задач юзать workflow`\n\n**Root cause of the 3000-line bloat:** one concept — \"a sell\" — was modelled twice. The `MarketSell` workflow both *placed* the order **and** *owned* the `market_listings` read model, threading a `wf_id` column through the table, repo, entity, protocol type, and dispatcher to keep the two in sync. Every path that touched a listing had to ask \"is there a live workflow for this row?\".\n\nCollapsed onto **one rule, expressed in types instead of comments** — this is the answer to \"when to use a workflow vs not\":\n\n> - **A workflow is a durable *command*** — multi-step, side-effecting, survives restart, compensatable. *Placing a sell* is a command → `MarketSell`.\n> - **A poller is an idempotent *projection*** — periodically reflects external (Steam) state into a read model. *Tracking listings* is a projection → `ListingSync`.\n\nConsequences:\n\n- `MarketSell` is now a slim command (`Init → AwaitingConfirmation → Done`): place the order, accept the mobile confirmation, finish. It **never writes `market_listings`**; once the order is live it hands off via `ListingSync::require_sync`, so the poller is the table's **sole writer** — one source of truth.\n- The `wf_id` column is gone: entity, repo, protocol `Listing`, and the `m20260612_…_market_listings_wf_id` migration are removed. The dispatcher no longer clears `wf_id`; the API removes a listing directly instead of hunting for an owning workflow to abort.\n- `repo/market_listing.rs`: **224 → 141 lines**; `insert` is a single upsert on `listing_id` (the projection's only write path).\n- **Listings net change: 62 insertions / 456 deletions (−394).**\n\n---\n\n### Testing\n\n- `wf/tests/sell.rs` (new) drives `MarketSell` tick-by-tick on both paths (confirmation / no-confirmation). The confirmation path additionally **asserts `market_listings` stays empty** — a regression guard that encodes the command/projection boundary directly in a test.\n- The mock Steam server gains a deterministic, HTML-free market-sell flow (`sellitem` → `mobileconf` → `mylistings`).\n- Full workspace suite green locally:\n  - `cargo +nightly fmt --all --check` ✓\n  - `cargo +nightly clippy --workspace --all-targets --features ci --locked` ✓ (`-D warnings`)\n  - `cargo +nightly test --workspace --features ci --locked` ✓ (all tests, 0 failures)\n\n### Notes\n\n- Backend-focused per the issue; the webui is supported (wire format unchanged) but not reworked.\n- Push only to `issue-1-3d5965585644`; base branch is `listing-workflow`.\n"

Every path that touched a listing had to ask \"is there a live workflow for this row?\".\n\nCollapsed onto **one rule, expressed in types instead of comments** — this is the answer to \"when to use a workflow vs not\":\n\n> - **A workflow is a durable *command*** — multi-step, side-effecting, survives restart, compensatable. *Placing a sell* is a command → `MarketSell`.\n> - **A poller is an idempotent *projection*** — periodically reflects external (Steam) state into a read model. *Tracking listings* is a projection → `ListingSync`.\n\nConsequences:\n\n- `MarketSell` is now a slim command (`Init → AwaitingConfirmation → Done`): place the order, accept the mobile confirmation, finish. It **never writes `market_listings`**; once the order is live it hands off via `ListingSync::require_sync`, so the poller is the table's **sole writer** — one source of truth.\n- The `wf_id` column is gone: entity, repo, protocol `Listing`, and the `m20260612_…_market_listings_wf_id` migration are removed. The dispatcher no longer clears `wf_id`; the API removes a listing directly instead of hunting for an owning workflow to abort.\n- `repo/market_listing.rs`: **224 → 141 lines**; `insert` is a single upsert on `listing_id` (the projection's only write path).\n- **Listings net change: 62 insertions / 456 deletions (−394).**\n\n---\n\n### Testing\n\n- `wf/tests/sell.rs` (new) drives `MarketSell` tick-by-tick on both paths (confirmation / no-confirmation).
